title: Dialogue in its own block, speaker named
rule: Write each spoken line in a separate dialogue block, never inside the scene description, naming the speaker and a speech verb for every line.
why: Models tie a line to a face and gestures by the speaker label; mixing lines into description blurs who talks.
how: "Dialogue: The old man says, in English, ..." then the next speaker; same label spelling every time.

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js composeClip (Dialogue: line with who says, in <speech>)

title: Fit lines to the clip length
rule: Keep each speaker turn to about 12 words or fewer and put only as many lines in a clip as its seconds can hold (one or two short exchanges in 4 s).
why: Long lines get rushed, cut off or lose sync; vendors and guides agree on short turns.
how: Count words per line; if an 8 s clip has more than two turns, move the extra turn to the next clip.

monofilm.where: dialogue_load in get_clip warns when a clip has too many words for its length
monofilm.idea: Show the warning on the Brief page

title: Always state the audio policy, including silence
rule: Give every clip an explicit audio line (dialogue only, ambient only, or none), including clips meant to be silent.
why: When a prompt says nothing about sound the model fills it with plausible music, voices or extra lines.
how: "Audio: none. No speech, no voices, no music." for a silent clip.

title: Describe silence with concrete sound, not only bans
rule: For a clip with no speech, also name the real ambient sound and a closed mouth or a character alone, instead of relying only on "no talking".
why: Negative words can plant the idea of speech, and the model pads the whole clip with sound; a concrete soundscape gives it something else to fill.
how: "Fridge hum and soft rain; she keeps her mouth closed and is alone in the room."

monofilm.where: public/js/wizard-model.js AUDIO_TEXT: quiet room tone and closed mouths instead of a list of bans

title: Remove words that imply speech or a score
rule: Check the clip text for trigger words (interview, crowd, announcing, epic, montage, anthem) and replace them when the clip should not have speech or music.
why: Such words suggest talking or a soundtrack to the model even when audio is not requested.
how: Swap "epic montage" for a plain description of the action.

monofilm.idea: Lint clip prompts for speech/score trigger words when audioPolicy is silent or ambient.

title: Restate the audio rules in every continuation clip
rule: Repeat the audio line in every clip, extension and bridge, because each one is generated fresh and the soundtrack can change at the seam.
why: Extension and bridge steps act like new generations; background sound and voice do not carry over.
how: Same "Audio:" sentence in every clip prompt of a scene.

monofilm.where: composeClip pushes AUDIO_TEXT into every clip prompt

title: Expect burned-in subtitles and check for them
rule: Add "no text on screen" and check each take for burned-in subtitles or gibberish text; regenerate or crop if found, and make real subtitles separately.
why: Veo-class models learned from videos with burned-in captions and often draw them when someone speaks; negative prompts help only partly.
how: Review step: one frame check at speech moments; re-roll rather than rewording endlessly.

monofilm.where: composeClip Look line ends with "no text on screen"; real subtitles in public/js/pack.js srt
monofilm.idea: Add a review check that flags text in frames of clips with dialogue.

title: Spoken lines in quotation marks with a speaker tag
rule: Write the spoken words in quotation marks after a speaker tag: A woman says, "We have to leave now."
why: Several guides use quotes to mark what is spoken versus described.
how: Keep one style across the film.

title: Spoken lines after a colon, without quotation marks
rule: If burned-in subtitles appear, try the Google form: speaker, verb, colon, then the line with no quotation marks.
why: Google's own guide shows lines without quotes, and a guide suspects quotes invite caption text.
how: The detective says: Your story has holes.

monofilm.idea: Make the quoting style a per-generator setting in GENERATORS and test on Veo.

title: Do not trust a native voice to persist across clips
rule: For a character who speaks in more than one clip, plan one separate voice pass (TTS or speech-to-speech) over all native dialogue, because native voices change between generations even with a fixed seed.
why: Voice and background sound are not carried between generations; extension does not fix it.
how: Export each clip's speech, convert with one saved voice, remix under the picture.

monofilm.where: get_clip.voices and pack voicePlan: a speaker with lines in more than one clip is routed to a separate voice
monofilm.idea: Generate or import the voice pass inside the studio

title: Lock one voice configuration per character
rule: Keep one voice ID, one stability setting and one note of tags per character for the whole film, and generate each character's lines in one session.
why: Switching tools or settings mid-series causes audible drift; batching makes drift show at once.
how: Store voice id, model, stability, pace beside the cast entry.

monofilm.idea: A locked voice configuration (voice id) per character

title: At most two speakers per clip
rule: Keep a generated clip to two speaking characters; split bigger conversations into clips per speaker pair.
why: Three or more speakers produced wrong voice attribution and drift after about 5 to 6 s in Kling 2.6.
how: Shot A: A and B; shot B: B and C.

monofilm.where: dialogue_load warns about more than two speakers in a clip
monofilm.idea: Block it on the Brief page

title: Use an audio-driven model for long monologues
rule: For a speech longer than one generation, feed the finished voice track to an audio-driven model (Wan2.2-S2V, InfiniteTalk, OmniHuman) that makes video of a still character for as long as the audio.
why: Output length follows the audio, so no clip joins are needed in the talking part; the voice is already fixed.
how: Reference picture plus WAV; check hardware and licence first (S2V needs 80 GB VRAM).

monofilm.idea: Offer a talking-shot route in the pack for scenes that are one long speech.

title: Use post lip-sync only to dub, not to rescue weak takes
rule: Use a post lip-sync tool when the speech was replaced (new voice or language), on near-frontal, well-lit faces with a clear mouth and clean single-speaker audio.
why: These tools change only the lip and lower-face area, so they cannot fix wrong gestures; they drift or distort on profiles and occlusions.
how: Check the chunk joins; split long clips; try the pro tier for teeth and beards.

monofilm.idea: Document as a fallback step after a voice swap.

title: Prefer native audio when the voice is not replaced
rule: If the native voice is acceptable, keep it and skip post lip-sync, because mouth-only editing leaves face and body out of step with the sound.
why: The InfiniteTalk authors argue mouth-only dubbing causes mismatched expression and gesture; no measured comparison with native audio exists in the sources.
how: Decide per scene: voice swap needed means audio-driven model or lip-sync; otherwise native.

monofilm.where: Studio generates speech natively in the clip prompt (composeClip Dialogue), no post lip-sync

title: Fill silent clips with video-to-audio foley
rule: For clips that must be silent of speech, add foley with a video-to-audio model (MMAudio, HunyuanVideo-Foley, ThinkSound) from the picture and a short sound description.
why: These models make effects aligned with on-screen events; HunyuanVideo-Foley outputs 48 kHz.
how: Describe the sound of the action in the text input.

title: Check the licence before using an audio model on a film
rule: Before using a generated sound or score in a released film, check the model licence and platform terms (MMAudio weights are non-commercial; Suno free tier is non-commercial).
why: Licence terms differ sharply between models and tiers and can change.
how: Record the model, version and licence beside each audio file.

monofilm.idea: Add audio files with provenance to the film pack manifest.

title: Add ambience and music in post when native audio is thin
rule: Treat native audio as a guide track; add real ambience, effects and score in post when it sounds flat or metallic.
why: Reviewers found Sora 2 audio flat, muffled and unevenly balanced; the model cannot separate dialogue, effects and ambience.
how: Keep the native dialogue stem if possible and lay separate beds under it.

title: Duck music under speech and set one loudness target
rule: Mix score under dialogue with side-chain compression, then normalise the whole film with two-pass loudnorm to one chosen target.
why: FFmpeg offers sidechaincompress (defaults: threshold 0.125, ratio 2, attack 20 ms, release 250 ms) and loudnorm (defaults -24 integrated, -2 true peak); the right values depend on the delivery target.
how: Pass 1 measure, pass 2 with measured_* values; keep every clip on the same target.

monofilm.idea: Duck music under speech when there is a score

title: Join clips with a short audio crossfade at one sample rate
rule: Join clip audio with a short crossfade and resample everything once to a common rate (48 kHz is the video standard) before the join.
why: Independent clips have different room tone and level; a hard cut gives a click or a gap. TTS output mostly stops at 44.1 kHz and effect or foley tools output 48 kHz, so mixed rates must be unified.
how: acrossfade with a duration of tens of milliseconds, then loudnorm on the whole.

monofilm.where: scripts/assemble-film.mjs fades each clip's sound in and out for a moment at one sample rate
monofilm.idea: A true crossfade with overlap where two clips clash

title: Use one looping ambience bed across a scene
rule: Generate one ambience bed (loop mode) per scene and lay it under all its clips, instead of using each clip's own background.
why: Background sound changes or stops at clip boundaries; loop effects have no audible start or end.
how: "Rain against a window in a quiet apartment", loop, 30 s max per file.

monofilm.idea: Scene sound note could drive an ambience file.

title: Subtitles: 5/6 to 7 seconds, two lines, UTF-8 SRT
rule: Write subtitles as SRT in UTF-8 with each cue at least 5/6 s and at most 7 s, at most two lines, broken at punctuation or before conjunctions.
why: These are Netflix limits; SRT has a fixed block form with a comma before milliseconds.
how: Split a long line into two cues; time each clip's cues from that clip's own start.

monofilm.where: public/js/pack.js srt (comma stamps, default 2 s, min 1 s, per-clip transcript.srt timed from clip start); no 7 s or two-line limit
monofilm.idea: Cap cue length at 7 s and wrap at two lines.

title: Say the language on every line and verify it was kept
rule: Name the spoken language in each dialogue line and check the take, because several models translate unsupported languages into English voice.
why: Kling 2.6 voices only English and Chinese; Seedance lists a wider set; TTS quality varies by language.
how: "says, in Spanish, ..."; if a language is unsupported, use separate TTS in that language.

monofilm.where: composeClip uses film.speech (", in <speech>,") and an English gloss in brackets

title: Describe the action that makes each sound; one dominant layer
rule: Name the exact sound source tied to a visible action, and keep to one dominant sound layer per clip.
why: Effects bind to on-screen events frame by frame; vague words ("noise") and competing layers confuse the sync.
how: "A wooden door slams shut with a loud bang" not "noise".

monofilm.where: notes.sound is passed as free text ("Sound: ...")
monofilm.idea: Writer hint that a sound note names source and action.

title: Clone a voice only with the owner's consent, and label synthetic speech
rule: Use a cloned voice only for the person it belongs to or with their verified consent, and label synthetic speech where law or platform requires.
why: ElevenLabs allows professional clones only of your own verified voice; the EU AI Act requires disclosure of audio deepfakes with a lighter duty for evidently artistic works.
how: Keep the consent record with the project; use stock or designed voices otherwise.

monofilm.where: pack publishing checklist item for synthetic voices
monofilm.idea: A consent field on a voice

title: Draft with audio off, test on a short clip
rule: Test dialogue prompts on a short, low-resolution clip first, and render with audio only for finals when the tool charges extra for it.
why: Audio doubles cost in Kling 2.6 Professional mode, and prompt problems show in a short test.
how: Draft silent; add audio for the approved prompt.
